A1.justification: Both supplied 11-page PDFs describe the same work and are fully readable, including their figures, tables and equations. Neither contains an appendix, despite references to supplementary material. All supplied pages support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-world and simulated robot experiments, VLM comprehension evaluations, and ablations in Section 6 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including robot task success rates, comprehension scores, drawing-style comparisons and keypoint-localization measurements.

M1.justification: The RoVI primitives and VIEW procedure remain unchanged: VLM planning, YOLOv8 keypoint extraction and keypoint-conditioned robot control. Figure 3's revised terminology does not change the algorithm described in Sections 3 and 5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 15K-instance RoVI Book dataset derived from Open X-Embodiment and evaluate the same eight real-world and three simulated manipulation tasks. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains VoxPoser and CoPa for real-world comparisons and RT-1-X, Octo-goal-image and Octo-language for simulation. The VLM comparators in Section 6.3 and detector comparators in Table 4 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the same training configurations, robot hardware, SIMPLER/SAPIEN setup and evaluation procedures. Action success, spatiotemporal alignment, task/planning assessment and keypoint-localization metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same trajectory comparison, language-response error breakdown, drawing-style study and keypoint-module analysis in Figures 8–10 and Tables 3–4. No analysis is added, removed or revised.

E5.justification: Both retain the ten-trial evaluations, Figure 8's sampling of six successful trajectories from 50 trials, and Table 4's identical ± reporting. No seed information or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and graphical results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains real-world averages of 82.5% for VIEW-GPT4o and 87.5% for VIEW-LLaVA-13B, and the shared simulated VIEW average of 76.6%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same arrow representation, VLM mapping, control objective and rotational-angle calculation. No mathematical definition, derivation, assumption or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about RoVI, VIEW, the training dataset and generalization. Removing 'three-dimensional' from one introductory summary does not alter the retained 2D-to-3D manipulation claim.

C2.justification: The explanations involving language ambiguity, symbol-based keypoint robustness, color-guided temporal decomposition and comprehension-versus-execution errors remain unchanged. The future-work discussion and references to supplementary limitations are also retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link beneath the affiliations and replaces the abstract's promise that code and datasets will be released soon with that link. This changes resource-access information; the PDFs do not establish that code or data were actually released. Implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 retains the same positioning against language-conditioned, image-conditioned and keypoint-based approaches. The same 52 references remain, with no added or removed cited works.

P1.justification: Limited wording edits remove 'three-dimensional' from one introductory sentence and change Figure 3's 'language-to-action' to 'sketch-to-action'. The section order and substantive exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page title block adds the project link and moves the corresponding-author note inline, with local text reflow. Figure 3's caption changes, but all embedded figure images remain identical. Pages 4–11 render identically.

improvement.justification: The project link and caption correction provide small access and clarity refinements, but v1 already clearly describes sketch-based input. Methods, evidence, substantive explanations and limitations remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish an actual code/data release. These limited edits do not demonstrate a meaningful overall quality difference.
